cards.title: Deploying Secure AI for UCCE and Private Cloud Environments
cards.text:
Deploying Secure AI for UCCE and Private Cloud Environments (Technical Training Class).
Scheduled:
- Monday, October 5, 9:15 AM to 10:15 AM CDT — Iris, Level 4 — session code CLS-21229 — 60 minutes — Class: Intermediate
Speakers: Rajiv Krishnan, Chandramouli Vaithiyanathan.
Topics: AI, Customer Experience, Contact Center, Platform/Architecture, Control Hub, Integrations.
About: Organizations running on-premises UCCE and private cloud environments face a critical challenge: how to adopt generative AI without compromising security, data sovereignty, or control. This session provides a technical and strategic framework for deploying AI agents in high-security contact center environments while preserving the integrity of existing infrastructure. We will explore four key areas. First, you'll learn how Customer Voice Portal (CVP) and existing call flows integrate with Cisco AI Studio, including the technical handoffs and orchestration between legacy logic and modern AI services. Next, you'll learn how to address data sovereignty and security by defining clear boundaries between private cloud environments and externally processed workloads to help close the trust gap. We'll then explore strategic AI orchestration and how to move beyond a single-bot model toward a multi-agent architecture. Topics include Silent Transfer, Announced Transfer and MCP handoffs, as well as how to establish boundaries for agent specialization. Finally, we'll cover governance and advanced observability, including how to implement Cisco's AI Impact Assessment framework to manage fairness and safety while proactively monitoring for hallucinations, accuracy drift, and system prompt changes. You'll leave with a clearer path for modernizing UCCE with secure, observable AI while maintaining control over infrastructure, data, and deployment-and a practical framework for bridging legacy reliability with autonomous customer experience. CE credits: 2

Topics: Customer Experience, Calling, Devices, Contact Center, Platform/Architecture, Integrations.
About: This technical session explores the architecture and capabilities of a unified Webex platform. We will examine how Webex Contact Center and Webex Calling streamline infrastructure, simplify deployments, and power seamless customer experiences. We will begin with a brief overview of today’s Webex Contact Center Common Edge Services, followed by a quick look at future use cases that Webex Common Media Services will enable. The core of the session will focus on the technical mechanics of Webex Contact Center Common Edge Services. We will dive deep into PSTN and routing options including Cloud Connected PSTN (CCP) and Bring Your Own PSTN (BYOPSTN). We'll cover the Edge Connect architecture to bring media to Webex using private link, as well as global deployment strategies with a spotlight on supporting operations in India. Finally, we will cover key cross-platform integrations designed to optimize operations. You will learn about advanced reporting that captures Webex Calling call legs, Webex Calling device control, WebRTC enhancements, and Webex Messaging for agent-to-supervisor collaboration. We will conclude with roadmap highlights. CE credits: 2

And if allyship never asks anything of us, is it really allyship? Join women leaders from akamai, M&T Bank, and Cisco for a candid conversation about what leadership has asked women to become, what women have changed for everyone, what real allyship requires, and the choices we have to make now if we want the future of work to be meaningfully different from the past. The future of leadership isn't something women are waiting to be included in. We're already helping build it.

Bobby McGonigle Jr — Technical Marketing Engineer, Cisco.
Category: Cisco (TRAINING SESSION SPEAKERS).
Bio: I’m a Technical Marketing Engineer in Cisco’s Devices Business Unit, focusing on RoomOS products designed for integrators, including the Codec Pro G2 and Codec EQ. My interest in collaboration technology began during a university internship, where my first exposure to professional audiovisual systems centered on Cisco. I was hooked. I’m now in my fifth year at Cisco, where I specialize in RoomOS xAPIs, macros, and room design. Before joining Cisco, I spent four years supporting RoomOS devices in education, an environment where complex technology needs to feel simple and natural for teachers. That experience still shapes my work today. I like to think of myself as a Cisco customer with a little extra access, helping make a product I already love even better. One project I’m especially proud of is the Join Zoom macro. I originally created it at the university to make joining Zoom SIP meetings easier for my users, then shared it with the wider Cisco community. After joining Cisco, I had the opportunity to watch that idea evolve into an official product capability. The final implementation was not my code, but it solved the same problem and reflected the user experience I had set out to create. The macro has since been retired in favor of the current Join Zoom solution, but I’m proud that something I built for my users served the wider community and lived a full life. That journey captures what I enjoy most about RoomOS. I want to help people discover what they can create with it. My goal as a speaker is to take people with little or no coding or xAPI experience and give them the confidence to interact with RoomOS devices like professionals.

cards.title: Jeetu Patel
cards.text:
Jeetu Patel — President & Chief Product Officer, Cisco.
Category: Cisco Keynote (KEYNOTE SPEAKERS).
Bio: Jeetu Patel is Cisco’s President and Chief Product Officer. He combines a bold vision, steeped in product design and development expertise, operational rigor, and innate market understanding to create high growth businesses. He is relentlessly focused on building world class products that solve Cisco customers’ biggest problems—bringing the power of the Cisco portfolio together to connect and protect every aspect of their organization in the era of AI. Previously he was Cisco’s Executive Vice President and General Manager of Security and Collaboration where he led the strategy and development for these businesses and held P&L responsibility for the multibillion-dollar portfolio. In this role, Jeetu led with his creative vision and intense focus on innovation and swift execution. Together with his team, he transformed and positioned our Security and Collaboration portfolios for success and growth. In both areas, he reinvigorated organic innovation, championed key inorganic investments, and drove simplification across these portfolios with a fanatical focus on design and user experience. Prior to joining Cisco in 2020, Jeetu was the Chief Product Officer (CPO) and Chief Strategy Officer (CSO) at Box, a role he pioneered. He led the company’s product and platform strategy, setting the company’s long-term vision and roadmap for cloud content management in the enterprise. He transformed Box from a single product application to a multi-product platform used by 100K customers representing 69% of the Fortune 500. The discipline, quality standards, performance metrics, and stability Jeetu instilled fueled the platform’s growth – nearly quadrupling revenues to $700M+. Box’s growth scaled to reach over 60M users with over 50% of customers using multiple products. He also created the Box Platform business unit where he led product strategy, marketing and developer relations – driving products from incubation stage to mature offerings. Before joining Box, Jeetu was General Manager and Chief Executive of EMC’s newly acquired Syncplicity business unit, a cloud service for Enterprise File Sync Sharing (EFSS) and collaboration. One of the first SaaS-based solutions offered by EMC, Jeetu spearheaded the company’s acquisition. He created a world class leadership team, secured some of the market’s largest customers and led the group to become one of the fastest growing EFSS companies in a highly competitive market. Other key roles at EMC included CMO for the Information Intelligence Group and Chief Strategy Officer, where he drove the organic and inorganic strategy for the division’s cloud and mobile growth. Previously, Jeetu was President of Doculabs, a research and advisory firm co-owned by Forrester Research. The firm focused on collaboration and content management across a range of industries including financial services, insurance, energy, manufacturing, and life sciences. He currently serves on the board of JLL, an American commercial real estate services company. Jeetu holds a B.S. in Information Decision Sciences from the University of Illinois, Chicago, and lives in the San Francisco Bay Area with his family.
Speaking at:
- Opening Keynote: From Possibility to Progress: How AI Is Changing the Way We Work and Engage — Wednesday, October 7, 9:00 AM to 10:30 AM CDT — Manchester Ballroom, Level 5
- Post-keynote Executive Q&A — Wednesday, October 7, 11:15 AM to 12:00 PM CDT — Palm Park A, Level 7

cards.title: Tim Messenger
cards.text:
Tim Messenger — Team Manager, Unified Communications - Contact Center, Community Health Network.
Category: Community Health Network, Customer/Partner.
Bio: Tim Messenger has spent two decades supporting the telephony environment at Community Health Network. Prior to working in IT, Tim spent time doing low voltage cabling and phone system installation, as well as a few years working in Emergency Medicine before returning to the world of IT. Initially starting as a contractor at CHNw for the E911 location mapping project, then joining the Voice Services/UC Team as an analyst supporting Nortel, and eventually Cisco Call Manager and UCCX. In 2012, he accepted a position as a Contact Center analyst supporting the UCCE IP/IVR environment. Then assisted in the migration to UCCE CVP. In 2017, a specific Contact Center Team was created, with Tim as the manager. During this time, he and his team assisted in many environment upgrades, support, and enhancements. In 2024, CHNw began the process of building the first WxCC contact centers, setting the stage for a full migration from UCCE. Tim and his team migrated over 120 contact centers and over 400 IVRs as well as deploying centralized scheduling and triage for Primary Care practices. During this they also worked with Cisco and Presidio to develop the first deployment of WxCC AI for a pilot program for a rescheduling agent integrated with the existing practice IVRs. After the pilot was completed, the UC Contact Center Team deployed the AI Rescheduling Agent to an additional 50 practices. Currently, they are working on the next use cases covering New Appointment Scheduling, Registration, as well as Bill Pay/Payment Plans. Tim and his team continue to evolve to support the growing changes of the Contact Center world to help ensure the patients and care givers at Community Health Network have the best experience and care as possible.
Speaking at:
- The AI Concierge Advantage: Delivering Personalized CX at Scale — Wednesday, October 7, 1:30 PM to 2:00 PM CDT — Expo Theater, Level 3

cards.title: Opening Reception at WebexOne 2026
cards.text:
- The Opening Reception for WebexOne 2026 is on Tuesday, October 6, from 4:30 pm to 7:00 pm Central Time.
- Location: Congressional Ballroom, Level 3, Fairmont Austin.
- The event is open to all attendees.
- The Opening Reception kicks off the main conference and takes place in the Innovation & Solutions Showcase.
- Activities include networking with peers, meeting Cisco experts, connecting with sponsors and partners, exploring Cisco’s latest innovations, participating in interactive challenges, and enjoying Austin-inspired experiences.
- Professional portraits are available during the event.
- The WebexOne Expert Demo Showcase runs from 4:30 pm to 7:00 pm in the same area, with new demos every 15 minutes.
- Quick Take Sessions are held from 5:00 pm to 6:35 pm during the Opening Reception.
- The Covenant House Texas activity is available from 4:30 pm to 7:30 pm, where you can pack hygiene kits, meet the team, learn about their mission, donate, and hear about Cisco’s annual Sleep Out.
- Food is included at the Opening Reception.

cards.title: Capture the Flag Walk-in Lab Experience — How it works and who can participate
cards.text:
- Capture the Flag (CTF) is a gamified, hands-on, self-directed lab experience at WebexOne 2026.
- The lab is available as a walk-in activity for Training Pass holders only; bring your training pass to participate.
- No advance or prior registration is required to join the Capture the Flag lab.
- CTF labs are open throughout the day on Monday, October 5, Tuesday, October 6, and Thursday, October 8, 2026, in Violet, Level 4.
- The labs provide hands-on technical experience aligned with WebexOne collaboration outcomes, featuring real Webex challenges.
- Participants can join at their convenience during designated training hours, select a technical lab, engage in learning and building activities, and earn points.
- The program is flexible, allowing attendees to fill schedule gaps or participate if they missed a scheduled lab.
- Top scorers on the leaderboard at the end of the program can win prizes, but labs are also valuable for skill enhancement even without competing for prizes.
- Participants can earn Cisco Continuing Education (CE) credits by completing challenges.
- The Capture the Flag lab is part of the Technical Training Program, which runs from Monday morning, October 5, to Thursday afternoon, October 8, 2026.

cards.title: Ground Transportation Options in Austin
cards.text:
- Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (AUS) is about 10 miles from Fairmont Austin, with an estimated 20-minute drive to the venue.
- Ground transportation options between AUS and downtown Austin include rideshares, taxis, rental cars, private transportation, shuttles, pedicabs, electric low speed vehicles, limousines, charter services, and public transit.
- Rideshare and taxi pickups at AUS are located under the Consolidated Rental Car Facility, near the Red Garage. Check the airport ground transportation page for current pickup instructions.
- Capital Metro (CapMetro) is Austin's public transit provider. CapMetro Route 20 connects AUS and downtown Austin. Use the CapMetro Trip Planner or app for current routes, fares, and service times.
- The CapMetro app can be used to buy passes and plan trips. CapMetro offers a network of bus routes throughout Austin.
- The CapMetro Bike Share app allows you to rent electric bikes in central Austin.
- For more information on getting around Austin, visit https://www.austintexas.gov/department/getting-around-austin.

cards.title: WebexOne 2026 Training Overview
cards.text:
- The Technical Training Program at WebexOne 2026 is available to attendees with a Conference Pass + Training ticket.
- Training runs from Monday morning, October 5, through Thursday afternoon, October 8, 2026, for four days.
- Training includes technical classes and hands-on labs with guided walkthroughs.

  - Cisco Devices: Deep dive into intelligent video devices for various workstyles and workspaces.
  - Security, Identity, and Compliance: Best practices and design guidance for secure deployments, privacy, compliance, and protecting user identities.
  - Advanced Diagnostics and Troubleshooting: Expertise in Control Hub for investigating and pinpointing quality and configuration issues.
  - Integrations and Cross-Architecture Solutions: Using platform APIs and integrating with Cisco products like Meraki, ThousandEyes, Spaces, and more.
- Training is designed to help teams optimize deployments, unlock new features, minimize downtime, drive adoption, and onboard new users efficiently.
- New training courses will be available, covering the latest feature releases and best practices.
- For more details, view the agenda at https://www.webexone.com/agenda.html.

cards.title: How to Choose and Manage Your Technical Training Labs and Classes
cards.text:
- Use the Technical Training Agenda Builder at https://reg.rainfocus.com/flow/webex/webexone2026/agendabuilder to select and manage your technical training labs and classes for WebexOne 2026.
- Log in with your registration email and password.
- The Agenda Builder opens September 10. All training attendees will receive the link and instructions by email.
- From September 10 at 11 am ET / 4 pm BST until September 16 at 11 am ET / 4 pm BST, you may reserve one lab to ensure equitable access.
- After September 16 at 11 am ET / 4 pm BST, the one-lab limit is lifted and you may add additional labs, subject to availability. You will receive a reminder email when this happens.
- Browse sessions by date, track, or topic, or search for a class or lab title. Use filters for My Favorites, My Sessions, Session Tracks, Session Topics, and Technical Depth.
- Click a session name to read the abstract, see speakers, and review details. Click 'Add to Schedule' to add a class or lab to your agenda.
- If a class or lab is full, starting September 16, you can click 'Add to Waitlist.' Waitlisting blocks that time slot on your agenda. You may leave the waitlist at any time. If space opens, you’ll be added and notified by email in waitlist order.
- New waitlist additions close Sunday, October 4 at 1 pm ET / 6 pm BST.
- Dropping a class or lab removes you from that session and releases the seat.
- You cannot add classes or labs that overlap in time.
- There is a 5-minute grace period after the scheduled start time; open seats are offered to waitlisted attendees.
- Use day/date labels to explore sessions from Monday, October 5 through Thursday, October 8.
- Click the heart icon to add a session to My Favorites (this does not add it to your agenda).
- All technical training selections and changes must be made in the Technical Training Agenda Builder. Your training agenda will be visible in the WebexOne app, but changes must be made in the Agenda Builder.
- For non-training sessions (keynotes, breakouts, roundtables, Quick Takes), use the WebexOne App at https://go.socio.events/e88l5.
- Check the full schedule at https://www.webexone.com/agenda.html.

- All Training pass holders may reserve one lab from September 10 at 11 am ET / 4 pm BST until September 16 at 11 am ET / 4 pm BST.
- Starting September 16 at 11 am ET / 4 pm BST, the one-lab limit is lifted and you may add additional labs on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to availability.
- Many labs may fill quickly; choose your preferred lab as soon as possible.
- A limited number of additional or repeat lab deliveries will be scheduled based on demand and available capacity.
- You will receive a reminder email when the lab limit lifts on September 16.
- All selections and changes for Training classes and labs must be made in the Technical Training Agenda Builder, accessible via your WebexOne 2026 Attendee Portal starting September 10.
- Your Training agenda will be visible in the WebexOne app, but all selections and changes must be made in the Technical Training Agenda Builder.
- The WebexOne app is used for building your agenda for keynotes, breakouts, roundtables, Quick Takes, and other non-training sessions.
- To select or manage labs and classes, log in to the Technical Training Agenda Builder at https://reg.rainfocus.com/flow/webex/webexone2026/agendabuilder using your registration email and password.
- You cannot add classes or labs that overlap with one another.
- If a class or lab is full, starting September 16 you can join the waitlist, which blocks that time slot on your agenda until you leave the waitlist.
- If space becomes available, you’ll be automatically added and notified by email based on waitlist order.
- New waitlist additions close Sunday, October 4th at 1 pm ET / 6 pm BST.
- There is a 5-minute grace period for attendance: 5 minutes after the scheduled start time, any open seats will be offered to waitlisted attendees.

cards.title: Training Lab Reservations and Waitlist Policies
cards.text:
- All Training pass holders may reserve one lab from September 10 at 11 am ET / 4 pm BST until September 16 at 11 am ET / 4 pm BST.
- Starting September 16 at 11 am ET / 4 pm BST, the one-lab limit is lifted and you may add additional labs on a first-come, first-served basis, as your schedule and class/lab capacity allow.
- Reservations and changes for training labs and classes must be made in the Technical Training Agenda Builder at https://reg.rainfocus.com/flow/webex/webexone2026/agendabuilder using your registration email and password.
- You cannot add classes or labs that overlap with one another.
- If a class or lab is full after September 16, you can click 'Add to Waitlist.'
- Waitlisting does not guarantee access. Joining a waitlist blocks that time slot on your agenda and prevents you from adding another class or lab at the same time unless you leave the waitlist.
- You may leave the waitlist at any time to free up your slot.
- If space becomes available, you’ll be automatically added and notified by email based on waitlist order.
- New waitlist additions close Sunday, October 4th at 1 pm ET / 6 pm BST.
- Dropping a class or lab from your agenda removes you from that session and releases the seat for others.
- There is a 5-minute grace period for attendance: 5 minutes after the scheduled start time, any open seats will be offered to waitlisted attendees in order.
- Onsite, if a class or lab is full, you may join the queue outside the room. After the waitlist is cleared, remaining seats may be offered to those in the queue.
- The Capture the Flag program allows a walk-in lab experience for Training pass holders.
- All selections and changes for training labs and classes must be made in the Technical Training Agenda Builder; the WebexOne app is for non-training sessions.

cards.title: Capture the Flag Labs at WebexOne 2026 — Description and Schedule
cards.text: Capture the Flag (CTF) labs at WebexOne 2026 are gamified, self-directed learning environments designed to provide hands-on technical experience aligned with WebexOne collaboration outcomes. CTF labs use a walk-in format during designated training hours, allowing Training pass holders to join at their convenience, select a technical lab, engage in learning and building activities, and earn points. No prior registration is required for CTF labs. The program is flexible, letting attendees fill schedule gaps or participate if they missed a scheduled lab. Participants who score highest on the leaderboard at the end of the program can win prizes, but the labs are also valuable for skill enhancement even without competing for prizes. CTF labs are only available to Training pass holders.

cards.title: Cisco Continuing Education Credits at WebexOne 2026 — How to earn and claim
cards.text:
- You can earn Cisco Continuing Education (CE) credits at WebexOne 2026 by completing classes and hands-on labs in the Technical Training Program.
- CE credits are available for each class and lab you attend; the number of credits for each is shown on the event website and in the Technical Training Agenda Builder within the WebexOne app.
- Capture the Flag, a gamified hands-on lab, also offers CE credits. No registration is needed, but you must have a Training Pass to participate.
- To qualify for CE credits, you must meet attendance requirements and hold an active Cisco certification at the associate, specialist, professional, or expert level.
- CE credits earned at WebexOne 2026 will be processed and should appear in your Cisco account within three to four weeks after the event.
- The CE Portal is moving to Cisco U. For updates, see: https://learningnetwork.cisco.com/s/blogs/a0DQO000007aaaV2AQ/ce-portal-is-moving-to-cisco-u
- For more information on the Cisco CE program, view the user guide: https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en_us/training-events/certifications/continuing-education-portal-guide.pdf
- For questions about CE credits and the training program, see the Training Program FAQs.
- You can build your training agenda at https://reg.rainfocus.com/flow/webex/webexone2026/agendabuilder.

cards.title: WebexOne 2026 Audience and Learning Opportunities
cards.text: WebexOne 2026 is open to everyone. The event features keynotes, breakout sessions with industry leaders, and AI visionaries. Attendees include business leaders, IT decision makers, IT administrators, HR representatives, facilities managers, developers, customer success professionals, and event professionals. The technical training program is designed for Webex customer and partner administrators and IT staff who manage solution architectures. Business & IT Leaders can learn from industry experts about agentic AI use cases. CX Leaders receive guidance from businesses using AI to optimize customer experience strategies. IT Administrators can get trained on new product releases, explore product roadmaps, and learn technical best practices. Partners have opportunities to network with the Cisco partner and customer community, see the latest product announcements, and learn how to position Cisco solutions. In 2025, the in-person audience by job level was: Engineer/Developer 29%, Manager 20%, Other 18%, Director 15%, VP 10%, C-Suite 8%. By industry: High tech (software & services, hardware & equipment) 28%, Telecommunications 19%, Other 10%, Financial services 9%, Professional services (accounting, consulting, legal) 9%, Health care/medical/pharma/biotech 8%, Education 3%, Manufacturing 3%, Government 2%, Retail 2%, Aerospace 1%, Automotive 1%, Diversified & conglomerate 1%, Energy/chemical/utilities 1%, Hospitality/travel/tourism 1%, Media/advertising/PR 1%, Transportation/distribution 1%. By country: United States 85%, EMEA 6%, Canada 3%, United Kingdom 3%, APJC 2%, Mexico 1%.

cards.title: Fairmont Austin Parking Information and Discounts
cards.text: WebexOne attendees at the Fairmont Austin can receive a 10% parking discount. Hotel guests should inform the Fairmont Austin front desk that they are attending WebexOne with Cisco to have the discount applied to their hotel folio. Non-hotel guests can request a parking discount voucher at the Registration & Information Desk. cards.title: WebexOne 2026 App Download and Support
cards.text:
Download the WebexOne 2026 app to build your personal agenda for all Keynotes, Breakouts, Roundtables, Quick Takes, and more event experiences. Discover speakers and sponsors, navigate the venue, connect on the Social Wall, receive important event updates, and make the most of your time at WebexOne.

cards.title: WebexOne 2026 Registration, Pass Types, and Hotel Information
cards.text:
WebexOne 2026 will be held at the Fairmont Austin from October 5-8, 2026. Registration options and pricing are as follows:

- Conference Pass: Early Bird $599 (May–July 17), Advance $699 (July 18–September 4), Last Chance $799 (September 5–October 8).
- Conference Pass + Training (includes full event, technical training classes, and hands-on labs): Early Bird $999 (May–July 17), Advance $1,099 (July 18–September 4), Last Chance $1,199 (September 5–October 8).
- Access to the Technical Training Program requires a Training pass. There are no ticket options for training & hands-on labs only. Training passes have historically sold out, so early registration is recommended.
- Virtual Pass: Free. Includes live & on-demand access to keynotes, virtual sponsor & speaker content, Social Wall, and more. Breakout sessions, technical training, and hands-on labs are not included with the Virtual Pass.

The group rate at the Fairmont Austin is $295/night plus taxes and fees. The venue has a limited number of rooms and cannot accommodate all attendees. Early hotel booking is highly recommended. Austin City Limits, a major music festival, takes place before and after WebexOne, so hotel rooms in the area may be limited.

cards.title: Building Your Personal Agenda and App Support at WebexOne 2026
cards.text:
You can build your personal agenda for WebexOne 2026 using the WebexOne app on your phone, tablet, laptop, or browser. Select 'Agenda' from the main page to browse Keynotes, Breakouts, Roundtables, Quick Takes, and more. To add a session, click the plus (+) icon next to it. Click into each session for more details, including location, description, and speakers. View your selections by choosing 'My Agenda' at the top of the Agenda page. Only one item can be added per time slot. It is recommended to leave meals off your Personal Agenda to save those slots for sessions. 

Training Pass holders must use the Technical Training Agenda Builder to select or update technical training classes and labs. Your training schedule will appear in the WebexOne app, but changes must be made in the Agenda Builder, not the app. 

The WebexOne AI Concierge is available in the app starting Sunday, October 4. It provides session recommendations, speaker info, schedule guidance, venue navigation, and answers to most event-related questions. 

If you have trouble signing in, contact your IT administrator for SSO issues. If unresolved, contact WebexOne Registration Support to update your registration with a personal email address.

cards.title: Resetting Your WebexOne 2026 Account Password
cards.text:
To reset your WebexOne 2026 account password:
- Go to https://reg.rainfocus.com/flow/webex/webexone2026/attendee/login and click the "Forgot Password?" link.

cards.text: After registering for WebexOne 2026, your confirmation will include an automatic payment receipt. You can also access your ticket receipt via the WebexOne Attendee Portal. cards.title: How to Choose and Manage Your Technical Training Labs and Classes
cards.text: To select your specific training labs and classes for WebexOne 2026, log in to the Technical Training Agenda Builder at https://reg.rainfocus.com/flow/webex/webexone2026/agendabuilder using your registration email and password. Browse sessions by date, track, or topic, or search for the class or lab title. Click a session name to read the full abstract, see the speakers, and review session details. Click 'Add to Schedule' to add a class or lab to your personal agenda. If a class or lab is full, starting September 16th, you can click 'Add to Waitlist.' Waitlisting does not guarantee access and blocks that time slot on your agenda, preventing you from adding another class or lab at the same time unless you leave the waitlist. You may leave the waitlist at any time. If space becomes available, you’ll be automatically added and notified by email based on waitlist order. New waitlist additions close Sunday, October 4th at 1 pm ET / 6 pm BST. Dropping a class or lab from your agenda removes you from that session and releases the seat for others. You cannot add classes or labs that overlap with one another. Many labs and some classes have full enrollments and waitlists. There is a 5-minute grace period for attendance: 5 minutes after the scheduled start time, any open seats will be offered to waitlisted attendees. Use the day/date labels to explore sessions from Monday, October 5th through Thursday, October 8th. Use filters for My Favorites, My Sessions, Session Tracks, Session Topics, and Technical Depth. Click the heart icon to add a session to My Favorites; this does not add it to your agenda but helps you save options. Technical training selections and updates must be made in the Technical Training Agenda Builder. Check the Agenda Page at https://www.webexone.com/agenda.html for the full schedule.

WebexOne 2026 will be held October 5–8, 2026 at the Fairmont Austin. The agenda is live and can be viewed at https://www.webexone.com/agenda.html. Additional sessions and speakers will be added soon. The day-by-day session schedule will be available on September 10.

In-person programming:
- Technical Training program: Monday, October 5 at 8 AM to Thursday afternoon, October 8.
- Main conference: Opening Reception on Tuesday evening, October 6; ends Thursday afternoon, October 8.

Virtual programming:
- Virtual program: Wednesday morning, October 7 to Thursday afternoon, October 8.

Live Stream Schedule (all times Central Daylight Time):
- Wednesday, October 7, 9:00 – 10:30 am: Opening Keynote
- Thursday, October 8, 9:00 – 10:15 am: Morning Keynote
- Thursday, October 8, 2:00 – 3:10 pm: Closing Keynote (Webex Customer Awards & Fireside Chat with Tom Brady)

cards.title: Fairmont Austin Hotel Block and Group Rate
cards.text: The attendee room block at the Fairmont Austin for WebexOne 2026 is now sold out. The Fairmont Austin is located at 101 Red River St, Austin, Texas, USA, 78701. The group rate was $295 per night plus taxes and fees. A three-night minimum stay was required for Conference Pass and Conference Pass + Training attendees. Attendees are responsible for all charges incurred during their stay, including room rates, taxes, and incidentals. The hotel may charge a deposit equivalent to the first night's room and tax after September 17, 2026, to the card provided at booking. Reservations must be canceled at least five days prior to arrival to avoid forfeiting the first night's deposit. For questions, contact the Support Team at webexone@external.cisco.com or call toll-free 855-420-2368 or local 408-940-8062. Contact Center Hours: September 7 – September 18: 9 am – 5 pm ET; September 21 - October 6: 9 am – 6 pm ET; October 7 and October 8: 9 am – 5 pm ET.

cards.title: WebexOne 2026 Featured Launches and Innovations
cards.text:
At WebexOne 2026, Cisco is introducing several new launches across four main areas:

- Intelligent workspaces: New features include RoomOS devices, enhanced room audio, more platform choices, improved booking, and better observability. Featured launches are Ceiling Speaker Pro, Google Meet integration, AI Device Agent, and Divisible Rooms.
- Webex Suite: Focused on an AI-first work experience, calling modernization, agent enhancements, and an open ecosystem. Featured launches include the AI-first Webex App, Cloud Intelligence for UCM, Personal Call Agent, and the MCP ecosystem.
- Customer experience: Emphasizes agentic customer journeys, trustworthy AI operations, and a blended workforce. Featured launches are Project Phoenix, AI Agent 360, SharePoint connector, and Native WEM.
- Cross-Cisco platform: Provides a unified operating view across collaboration, network, and observability. Featured launches are Cisco Cloud Control and AI Canvas with ThousandEyes and Meraki.

cards.title: WebexOne 2026 Training Agenda and Scheduling
cards.text: Training pass holders can add as many training classes to their agenda as the schedule and class capacity allow, but cannot add overlapping classes or labs. To explore available sessions from Monday, October 5th through Thursday, October 8th, click on the day/date labels. Use filters such as My Favorites, My Sessions, Session Tracks, Session Topics, and Technical Depth to narrow your options. Adding a session to My Favorites (by clicking the heart icon) does not add it to your agenda, but helps you save classes and labs to consider or waitlist later. Technical training selections and updates must be made in the Technical Training Agenda Builder. The full schedule with days and times is available on the Agenda Page. The WebexOne App is used to build your agenda for keynotes, breakouts, roundtables, Quick Takes, and other non-training sessions. All attendees will receive an email with instructions for building their personalized experience in the WebexOne app.

cards.title: Capture the Flag Labs at WebexOne 2026
cards.text: Capture the Flag (CTF) labs at WebexOne 2026 are gamified, self-directed learning environments designed to provide hands-on technical experience aligned with WebexOne collaboration outcomes. These labs use a walk-in format during designated training hours, allowing participants to join at their convenience, select a technical lab, engage in learning and building activities, and earn points. The program is flexible, letting learners fill schedule gaps or participate if they missed a scheduled lab. Participants who score highest on the leaderboard at the end of the program can win prizes. The labs are also valuable for anyone looking to enhance their skills, regardless of competition.

cards.title: Government/Public Sector Pricing and Training Access
cards.text: The Government/Public Sector Conference Pass + Training for WebexOne 2026 costs $649. To receive this pricing, select a Government option in the 'What industry are you in?' drop-down during registration. Cisco complies with all gifting and discount regulations for Government and Public Sector accounts. No additional discount codes can be applied to these passes, and all pricing must follow Cisco's Gift, Travel, and Entertainment (GTE) Policy. Cisco Learning Credits (CLCs) cannot be used to pay for any WebexOne 2026 tickets. Access to the technical training program and hands-on labs requires purchase of a Conference Pass + Training ticket. Standard Conference Passes, Virtual Passes, and On-Demand Passes do not include access to training or labs. Training sessions and hands-on labs are only available for in-person attendees at the event and are not offered virtually.

cards.title: Transportation and Parking in Austin for WebexOne 2026
cards.text: CapMetro is the public transportation provider in Central Texas. Download the CapMetro app to buy passes and plan trips. CapMetro offers a network of bus routes throughout Austin, including service to and from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (AUS). Ground transportation options at AUS include taxis, rideshare, shuttles, pedicabs, electric low speed vehicles, limousines, and charter services. For bicycling, visit the Bicycle Program webpage for route maps and safety tips. The CapMetro Bike Share app lets you rent electric bikes in central Austin. For downtown parking, visit the Parking Enterprise webpage for information on the Affordable Parking Program, parking meter enforcement times, and a map of downtown parking lots and garages. The Downtown Parking Map shows available parking garages and surface lots in the downtown area.

cards.title: Vinod Muthukrishnan Speaker Bio
cards.text: Vinod Muthukrishnan joined Cisco through the acquisition of CloudCherry, a startup he co-founded and led as CEO. This acquisition laid the foundation for Webex Experience Management. He has held leadership roles at Uniphore and Webex Contact Center, focusing on innovation in AI and CPaaS. Vinod is a former Merchant Marine officer and an early pioneer in mobile trading. He mentors founders, serves on the SaaSboomi Governing Council, and co-chairs the USISPF Startup Connect Program. Vinod lives in the Bay Area with his family and a vocal Husky, and spends weekends strategizing cricket plays with his amateur league team.

cards.title: Cisco Speakers: Brian Stout and Christian Bigsby
cards.text: Brian Stout leads Cisco’s Global Collaboration Sales and Go-to-Market organization. He is responsible for the Collaboration product sales specialists, inside sales, pre-sales engineering, channel and ecosystem strategy, and routes to market. Cisco Collaboration’s $6B business is a critical part of Cisco’s overall SaaS transformation plan and is one of Cisco’s most competitive market segments. Brian and his team are helping to redefine Cisco’s SaaS business strategy to bring subscription-based solutions to customers and partners. During his Cisco career, Brian has held several strategic sales roles, including Enterprise Account Manager for the financial industry, Director of Operations in the Americas leading the Commercial Segment, and leader of the Americas Collaboration Sales team. He is now Vice President of the Global Collaboration Sales organization. Christian Bigsby is SVP, Workplace Resources at Cisco.

cards.title: Technical Training Program at WebexOne 2026
cards.text: The Technical Training Program at WebexOne 2026 is available to attendees with a Conference Pass + Training ticket. This program provides access to 4 days of technical training classes and hands-on labs. Participants can earn Cisco Continuing Education (CE) credits. Training covers the Webex and Cisco Collaboration portfolio, including Contact Center, CPaaS, Webex Suite, Calling, Cisco Devices, and Control Hub. Attendees can participate in hands-on labs that include guided tours of Cisco and Webex products, focusing on key features, configurations, customizations, troubleshooting, and integrations. New training courses will be available, covering the latest feature releases and best practices. For more details, view the agenda at https://www.webexone.com/agenda.html.

cards.title: Jeetu Patel's Background and Achievements
cards.text: Jeetu Patel joined Cisco in 2020. Before Cisco, he was the Chief Product Officer (CPO) and Chief Strategy Officer (CSO) at Box. At Box, he led product and platform strategy, set the long-term vision and roadmap for cloud content management, and transformed Box from a single product application to a multi-product platform. Under his leadership, Box grew to 100,000 customers, including 69% of the Fortune 500, and scaled to over 60 million users. Revenues nearly quadrupled to over $700 million, and more than 50% of customers used multiple products.

cards.title: Cisco Desk Pro G2 Overview
cards.text: The Cisco Desk Pro G2 is a premium 27-inch touch collaboration device designed for executive desks and small huddle spaces. AI Agents for Webex Suite

PORTFOLIO ROLE Specialized agentic teammates for collaboration.

WHAT IT IS A family of specialized agents announced for Webex Suite—including Notetaker, Task Agent, Polling Agent, Meeting Scheduler, and Receptionist—to help complete defined collaboration workflows.

BEST FOR Organizations exploring how agentic teammates can reduce coordination work around meetings and team collaboration.

KEY CAPABILITIES

Notetaker for meeting capture and summaries.

Task Agent for turning conversation into tracked work.

Polling Agent for dynamic audience engagement.

Meeting Scheduler and Receptionist for coordination and guest experiences.

DISTINGUISH FROM Do not confuse this family with Webex AI Agent for customer self-service or AI Receptionist for Webex Calling.

AVAILABILITY NOTE Publicly announced in the Fall 2025 release as “coming soon.” The concierge must use the approved WebexOne 2026 launch record for current availability.

Vidcast

PORTFOLIO ROLE Asynchronous video collaboration.

WHAT IT IS A video messaging tool for recording and sharing updates, presentations, demonstrations, and knowledge without scheduling a live meeting.

BEST FOR Status updates, executive communications, walkthroughs, training, demonstrations, and distributed teams working across time zones.

KEY CAPABILITIES

Record and share video through links or collaboration spaces.

Replace some meetings with watch-on-demand communication.

AI-assisted chapters, highlights, and summaries where available.

Embed video in websites, wikis, and workflows.

DISTINGUISH FROM Use Webex Meetings when real-time discussion is the point; use Vidcast when the message can be consumed asynchronously.

CONCIERGE-READY ANSWER Vidcast helps teams communicate with video without finding a time for everyone to meet. A person can record an update or walkthrough, share it, and let viewers catch up on demand—complete with AI-assisted navigation where enabled.

Sources: [2], [12]

Webex Webinars

PORTFOLIO ROLE Structured, interactive one-to-many experiences.

WHAT IT IS A scalable webinar service for polished virtual presentations with managed roles, registration, branding, audience engagement, interpretation, and webcast options.

BEST FOR Product launches, town halls, training, thought leadership, and large virtual programs where presenters lead and the audience participates in controlled ways.

KEY CAPABILITIES

Registration, branding, rehearsal, stage management, and presenter controls.

Moderated Q&A, chat, reactions, polling, and integrations such as Slido.

Breakouts, interpretation, captions, and translation options.

DISTINGUISH FROM Use Webex Meetings for highly collaborative many-to-many work; use Webex Events for an end-to-end conference or event program.

CONCIERGE-READY ANSWER Webex Webinars is built for polished, interactive broadcasts at scale. Hosts can manage the stage and presenters while still involving the audience through Q&A, polling, chat, reactions, and accessibility features.

Sources: [14]

Webex Events

PORTFOLIO ROLE End-to-end event management for in-person, virtual, and hybrid programs.

cards.title: Knowledge-base metadata and maintenance
cards.text:
Knowledge-base metadata and maintenance
Audience: WebexOne attendees ranging from first-time users to enterprise buyers, IT leaders, developers, workplace teams, CX leaders, partners, and media.

Freshness rule: revalidate product names and availability before the event, daily during major announcement windows, and after the event before reuse.

Source priority: approved WebexOne launch brief → official product page → current Webex Help Center → Cisco data sheet or developer documentation.

Conflict rule: prefer the newest approved source; preserve the older statement only as dated historical context.

Retrieval tags: product name, former name, acronym, portfolio family, user role, use case, industry, channel, deployment, session ID, speaker, venue, and status.

Answer length: default to 40–90 words; expand only when the attendee asks a follow-up.

Handoff triggers: pricing, contract terms, architecture, migration design, compliance commitments, roadmap dates, unsupported integrations, or customer-specific troubleshooting.

cards.title: Event narrative
cards.text:
Event narrative
WebexOne 2026 frames the event around “Connected Intelligence: Building the workplace of today, for the workforce of tomorrow.” The portfolio presents a shift from using AI to working with AI: people, assistants, and agents share context and move work forward across collaboration, customer experience, and the physical workplace.

AI that knows your work: context follows people across conversations and helps them prepare, understand priorities, and find what matters.

AI that gets work done: assistants, agents, skills, and connectors can complete supported tasks and multi-step workflows.

AI that works alongside you: agents can join spaces, meetings, and calls as teammates, while people stay responsible for judgment and decisions.

In customer experience, Cisco Dialog aims to move beyond linear journeys to a continuous relationship, with persistent context, long-running execution, rapid onboarding, and learning within enterprise policies.

In the workplace, RoomOS brings intelligence into rooms and devices; Cisco Cloud Control, AI Canvas, and AI Agent 360 extend visibility, action, and governance for IT and agent operators.
